name: KeepTrack (Mayer et al., ICCV 2021) - association of target and distractor candidates over time and confidence-aware memory management
bibliography: Christoph Mayer, Martin Danelljan, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool. Learning Target Candidate Association to Keep Track of What Not to Track. ICCV 2021 (peer-reviewed; CVF open access version). Preprint: arXiv:2103.16556 (v1 30 Mar 2021, v2 18 Aug 2021 = camera-ready content), DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2103.16556, HTML https://arxiv.org/html/2103.16556v2 . Code and trained models: https://github.com/visionml/pytracking (tracker: pytracking/tracker/keep_track/{keep_track.py, candidates.py}; parameters: pytracking/parameter/keep_track/default.py and fast variant; network: ltr/models/target_candidate_matching). Duplicates: the arXiv v2 and the ICCV paper are the same study. Base tracker is SuperDiMP (DiMP/PrDiMP family, pytracking), which is a separate study (see N03).
full_text_checked: Full HTML v2 read in two passes (method Sec. 3, Algorithm 1, training Sec. 3.x, Tables 1-3, 5, 7, 8, appendix Tables 9-11, Fig. 7 discussion); last ~16k characters of the appendix (VOT2018LT details, attribute plots) not read. Code: directory listing of pytracking/tracker/keep_track and full parameter file default.py read; keep_track.py and candidates.py source not read line by line. Table 9 and Table 1 checkmark columns were partly garbled in the HTML extraction.
task_and_output: Generic single-object tracking (short-term and long-term). Input: a first-frame bounding box of an arbitrary object. Output per frame: one bounding box (from SuperDiMP score map + IoU-Net refinement) plus a confidence score; in long-term protocols (OxUvA, VOT-LT) also a target present/absent decision derived from that confidence. Internally: a set of target candidates (local maxima of the classifier score map), a soft assignment matrix between candidates of the previous and current frame, persistent object ids for all candidates, and the id currently designated as target (or none).
data_and_independent_videos: Association network trained on LaSOT train (1120 sequences, split 1000 train-train / 120 train-val for development). Base SuperDiMP trained on its standard large datasets (LaSOT, GOT-10k, TrackingNet, COCO) and frozen. Evaluation on unseen test videos of separate benchmarks: LaSOT test (280 videos), LaSOTExtSub (150 videos, unseen classes), UAV123 (123), NFS 30 fps (100), OTB-100 (100), OxUvA (test via server, threshold set on OxUvA dev), VOT2019LT/VOT2020LT (50 long videos). Train and test videos are disjoint (LaSOT protocol split).
target_size_and_input_resolution: RGB crop of 480x480 px (search area scale 8 x target size; params.image_sample_size = 30*16), raised from 352 px (scale 6) in SuperDiMP. Classifier score map 30x30 with stride 16 px (inferred from 480/30; paper gives 22x22 -> 30x30). Target therefore occupies roughly 1/8 of the search width, about 3-4 score-map cells; distractors can appear anywhere in a window ~8x the target. Backbone ResNet-50 layer-3 features 29x29x1024 projected to 30x30x256 for candidate appearance.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: Benchmarks at native frame rate (mostly 25-30 fps; NFS evaluated at 30 fps); unconstrained handheld/drone camera motion and cluttered moving backgrounds; no ego-motion compensation. Search-area rescaling after occlusion averages the last up to 30 search areas.
detector_and_exemplar: No class detector. Target specified only by the first-frame box; online-learned SuperDiMP discriminative filter produces the score map; candidates are score-map maxima, not detector boxes. Exemplar is implicit in the DiMP memory (up to 50 samples).
trainable_nodes_and_loss: Trained: candidate encoder (MLP psi 3->32->64->128->256 on score and normalized position, added to a 2x2-conv projection of layer-3 appearance), 2 GNN layers (self- and cross-attention, SuperGlue-style), final 1x1 conv; Sinkhorn (10 iterations) with dustbin row/column is a differentiable layer without learned parameters except the dustbin score [uncertain]. Total parameter count not given in the read text. Loss: L_tot = L_sup + L_self; L_sup = -log A(l', l) for the annotated target candidate only (partial supervision, real data); L_self = sum of -log A over simulated identity correspondences (synthetic pairs: one frame, augmented copy with jittered positions, scores, brightness, blur, dropped candidates mapped to dustbin). ADAM lr 1e-4, x0.2 every 6 epochs, 15 epochs x 6400 sub-sequences, real:synthetic = 1:1. Real sub-sequences are mined (Table 9) to over-represent frames with several candidates, lost targets and wrong selection. Base SuperDiMP frozen (retrained without learned discriminative loss parameters).
controls_seeds_splits: Ablations against the same frozen SuperDiMP: memory confidence on/off, search area enlargement and rescaling, association on/off (Tables 1, 10), loss variants L_sup / L_self / both, with/without data mining (Table 2), memory weighting schemes (Table 3), number of GNN layers and Sinkhorn iterations including a 0-GNN variant (Table 11). Seeds: not reported for ablations (single runs; LaSOT numbers are typically averages of several tracker runs in pytracking but the text read does not state it) [uncertain]. Split: development on LaSOT train-val (120), final numbers on test benchmarks; OxUvA presence threshold set on OxUvA dev set. No confidence intervals.
metrics_and_numbers: Success AUC (%), from arXiv v2. Table 1 (NFS / UAV123 / LaSOT): baseline 64.7 / 68.0 / 65.0; + confidence and search area 65.2 / 69.1 / 65.8; + target candidate association (full KeepTrack) 66.4 / 69.7 / 67.1 -> association alone adds +1.2 / +0.6 / +1.3. Table 10 (appendix, components): none 64.4 / 68.2 / 63.5; memory confidence 64.7 / 68.0 / 65.0; + larger search area 65.3 / 68.4 / 65.5; + rescaling 64.7 / 68.4 / 65.8; full 66.4 / 69.7 / 67.1. Table 2 (LaSOT, association training): no association 65.8; L_sup only 66.0; L_self only 66.9; both, no mining 66.8; both with mining 67.1. Table 3 (LaSOT, memory): no confidence 63.5; confidence-based sample replacement 64.1; + online update threshold 0.0 64.6; threshold 0.5 65.0. Table 11 (NFS / UAV / LaSOT): 0 GNN + 50 Sinkhorn 65.9 / 69.2 / 66.6; 2 GNN + 10 Sinkhorn 66.4 / 69.7 / 67.1 at 18.3 FPS; 9 GNN + 50 Sinkhorn 66.4 / 69.8 / 67.2 at 12.7 FPS. Main results: LaSOT AUC 67.1 (Prec 70.2, NormPrec 77.2) vs SuperDiMP 63.1 (Table 5); KeepTrackFast 66.8 at 29.6 FPS; OxUvA MaxGM 80.9 (TPR 80.6, TNR 81.2); VOT2019/2020-LT F 70.9 (Pr 72.3, Re 69.7) (Table 7); UAV123 69.7, OTB-100 70.9 (SuperDiMP 70.1), NFS 66.4 (Table 8). Data mining categories (Table 9): single matching candidate 67.9% (text says 70%), highest-score candidate correct 18.4%, target score below threshold 0.3%, target visible but no candidate 2.8%, correct candidate not selected 1.5%, other 9.1%. Internal inconsistencies: Table 1 baseline LaSOT 65.0 vs Table 10 'none' 63.5 vs Table 5 SuperDiMP 63.1; text says memory confidence gives 1.5% on LaSOT (consistent with Table 10 63.5->65.0, not Table 1).
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: yes (LaSOT test, LaSOTExtSub unseen classes, other benchmarks). Target absence: yes (OxUvA TNR 81.2, VOT-LT precision/recall; target declared lost when its id has no candidate and redetection score < 0.25). Similar distractors: yes, the central motivation; qualitative Fig. 7 and LaSOT attribute analysis; no separate distractor-only benchmark like DiDi. Occlusion: yes (LaSOT/OxUvA full occlusion and out-of-view attributes; dustbin and search-area rescaling). Night or low light: not reported specifically beyond LaSOT 'illumination variation' attribute [uncertain]. Sequential operation on own predictions: yes, fully online; candidate ids and memory updates are driven by the tracker's own past outputs.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanism: (1) every local maximum of the score map above 0.05 is a candidate described by score, position and local appearance; (2) a learned graph network compares the candidate sets of the previous and current frame and a Sinkhorn optimal-transport layer with a 'no match' slot produces one-to-one matches; a match with probability >= 0.75 inherits the previous object id, otherwise a new id; ids without match disappear; (3) the target keeps its id while that id is visible; another object can take over only if its score exceeds every score in the target's own history; if the target id vanished, the best candidate becomes target only if its score >= 0.25, else target = none; (4) memory samples are weighted by a confidence (sqrt of max score when the selected object is the original id, raw score otherwise), the lowest age x confidence sample is replaced, and the online filter update ignores samples with confidence < 0.5; DiMP hard-negative updates when a distractor peak is high (distractor_threshold 0.8, hard_negative_learning_rate 0.02). Proposed modification for us (not published): replace learned ResNet appearance with FlyVis C/D activity sampled at each peak and keep the history-max switching rule and the dustbin.
transfer_limits: (a) Window geometry: KeepTrack's window is ~8x the target (480 px, target ~60 px, 30x30 map); ours is ~2x the target (721 hexals, target ~9x12 lattice steps). With a 2x window at most one target-sized object fits fully; distinct distractors mostly sit at the border, and secondary peaks are often parts of the same target or of a partially visible neighbour. KeepTrack's own statistics show 67.9% of frames already have a single candidate even with an 8x window; for us multi-candidate frames will be rarer and less distinct. (b) Features: candidate appearance is a 256-d projection of ResNet-50 layer-3 RGB features; we have 34 FlyVis cell types on 721 grey hexals, mostly motion/brightness-change signals; the 0-GNN ablation (66.6 vs 67.1 LaSOT) suggests the score/position/appearance encoding plus Sinkhorn carries most of the gain, so the learned GNN is not the critical part. (c) Moving and rescaling crop: our crop follows the Kalman prediction and rescales; candidate positions must be mapped to image coordinates between frames, otherwise the crop motion creates artificial displacements (KeepTrack also moves its window but encodes normalized positions inside it). (d) 30 Hz: matches KeepTrack's frame rates; but episodes of loss are at most ~30 frames, so the history-max rule has a short history. (e) Training data: needs many candidate-set pairs with a known target; our train26 (and 130 train videos) are small and repeatedly reused; synthetic self-supervision (augment one frame) is feasible without new annotation. (f) Environment: output feeds a centre correction before ByteTrack/MASA association, not a box; a held id on the wrong candidate still produces a wrong correction (case R1: 79.7 px shift).
research_questions_addressed: 5.1 (direct design evidence): separates 'target found' (target id still matched), 'similar distractor' (other ids, explicitly tracked), 'target outside/lost' (id unmatched, dustbin) and 'insufficient evidence' (redetection score < 0.25 -> none) by an explicit decision layer over tracked candidate ids, not by map maximum height alone; Table 1/10 show +1.3 LaSOT AUC from association. 5.2 (direct evidence): confidence-weighted memory and gated online updates (Table 3: 63.5 -> 65.0 LaSOT) protect the target model from distractor contamination. 5.3 (caution/indirect): the base feature extractor is frozen; association is trained on top - KeepTrack gives no evidence about training the core through the readout. 5.4 (analogy only): single-object; no MOT association or ID metrics.
candidate_node_change: Node: readout (candidate selection) plus memory write gate of the centred FlyVis readout. Change: (1) per frame of a loss episode extract all local maxima of the FlyVis target-model map (C or D) above a fixed fraction, describe each by [FlyVis activity vector at the peak (34 types, pooled over a small hexal neighbourhood), map score, position in image coordinates]; (2) learned light association (encoder MLP + Sinkhorn with dustbin; 0 or 1 attention layer, motivated by Table 11) between consecutive frames, trained by self-supervision on synthetic pairs from train videos (jittered copy of one frame) plus partial supervision from the annotated target; (3) KeepTrack decision rule: keep the target id while matched; switch only if another id exceeds the target's history-max score; if target id lost and no candidate >= redetection threshold, refuse (no correction); (4) write to the observation memory only when the selected id is the original id and confidence >= fixed threshold. Controls: no-FlyVis = identical pipeline with R1 (eye input, grey hexals) features and with geometry+score only (no appearance); stock FlyVis = same pipeline on stock C activity; plus the present centred readout top1 and Kalman-nearest. Minimal check: on train (fit20 for thresholds, then train26 frozen) useful-correction fraction per video with paired bootstrap; required C_assoc - C_top1 >= 2 p.p. with lower CI > 0 AND C_assoc - R1_assoc and C_assoc - geometry-only lower CI > 0; then refusal precision at fixed coverage (1/2/5%). Stop condition: if the learned association does not beat our already failed handcrafted Hungarian version (z13_candidate_identity_v1: C_assoc - C_top1 -3.29 p.p.) by the same criteria on train26, or if fewer than ~10% of loss frames contain >=2 distinct candidates (then the mechanism has nothing to act on in a 2x window), stop without dev/HOTA.
strongest_objection: We already ran the core of this idea (z13_candidate_identity_v1: causal one-to-one candidate identity propagation with missing option) and it was worse than the tallest peak (C -3.29 p.p. [-5.91; -0.89]) and not better than geometry (+0.76 [-1.39; +3.14]). KeepTrack's gains come from an 8x window with many distinct distractors and rich RGB appearance; in our 2x window with motion features the candidates are few, often not distinct objects, and FlyVis features may not discriminate the target from a neighbour of the same class. The learned GNN itself contributes little (Table 11: 66.6 without GNN vs 67.1), so 'learn the association' is not obviously what our failed version was missing.
evidence_strength: Moderate-strong for the published claim: peer-reviewed ICCV 2021, public code and models (pytracking, verified file listing and parameter file), widely re-used as a base (e.g., ToMP/MixFormer comparisons), several benchmarks with unseen test videos. Weak for transfer: single runs, no confidence intervals, gains of 0.5-1.3 AUC per component, internal table inconsistencies (baseline 65.0 vs 63.5 vs 63.1), and no evidence with small motion features.
where_distinction_is_made: In a separate decision layer over persistent candidate identities (Algorithm 1), fed by a learned association (representation + Sinkhorn with dustbin). 'Target found' = the target's id is matched in the current frame (regardless of whether it is the map maximum). 'Similar distractor found' = other ids exist and are tracked; a distractor with a higher map maximum does not take over unless its score exceeds all historical scores of the target id - this is exactly how a map maximum is separated from presence of the right object. 'Target outside search area / occluded' = target id matched to the dustbin; then redetection only if best score >= 0.25, else none. 'Insufficient data' is not modelled separately; it collapses into low score -> none and into memory confidence < 0.5 -> no update. The target model (DiMP filter) itself is distractor-aware only through hard-negative updates.
feature_dependence: Depends on rich RGB features: candidate appearance is a 256-d projection of ResNet-50 layer-3 features (29x29x1024) of a 480 px RGB crop, and the base SuperDiMP filter uses the same backbone. No experiment with motion-only or small features. Partial hint that appearance is not everything: the encoding adds score and position (psi MLP), the authors state that appearance alone can be insufficient and that position helps, while Fig. 7 notes failure when a distractor crosses the target (position useless). Transfer to 34 FlyVis types on 721 grey hexals is untested; our own z13_candidate_identity_v1 showed FlyVis appearance + distance did not beat geometry alone.
association_consequence: In KeepTrack the decision produces one box per frame; there is no detection matching. For us the chosen candidate becomes the centre correction before ByteTrack/MASA matching, so a refusal (none) keeps the Kalman prediction, and a kept-id choice changes the matching cost. The benefit for ID preservation would come from not switching to a neighbour (history-max rule) and refusing when the id is lost. An external guard rule could produce much of the same effect: limit the correction shift (e.g., reject corrections larger than a fraction of box size or that raise the IoU cost of the best detection above the gate, as in R1 where 0.123 -> 1.0 at gate 0.8), or a Kalman-gate on the corrected centre. This must be the required no-fly control.
difference_from_tried: Versus z13_candidate_identity_v1 (handcrafted alpha*cosine + distance/crop width, Hungarian with per-object missing cost, 3 peaks, expiring distractors, fitted on fit20): KeepTrack differs by (i) learned candidate encoding of score+position+appearance trained with self-supervised synthetic pairs and partial supervision, (ii) Sinkhorn soft assignment with a global dustbin and a match-probability threshold 0.75, (iii) all maxima above 0.05, not 3, (iv) the switching rule 'only if score exceeds the target's history maximum' (our version had no history-max rule), (v) explicit redetection threshold and none-output, (vi) confidence-gated memory write. Versus z13_candidate_ranker_v1 (learned ranking of 3 peaks per frame from activity): KeepTrack's choice is temporal (identity carried over frames), not a per-frame ranking. Versus z13_observed_memory_v1 / z13_query_memory_v1: KeepTrack's memory confidence gate (Table 3) is a write policy, which we did not test as such (we tested how memory is read). Honest summary: items (i)-(ii) are an upgrade of an implementation that already failed, not a new mechanism; (iv) and (vi) are genuinely untested by us.
memory_write_policy: Memory of up to 50 training samples for the DiMP filter. Each new sample gets confidence beta_t = sqrt(sigma) if the selected object has the original target id, else sigma (sigma = max score). When full, the sample with smallest age-weight x confidence is replaced (alpha_k = (1 - gamma) alpha_{k+1}). Online filter optimisation uses only samples with confidence >= 0.5 (params.certainty_for_weight_computation_ths = 0.5). Hard-negative updates with higher learning rate (0.02) when a distractor peak exceeds 0.8 (DiMP mechanism). Table 3: 63.5 (no confidence) -> 64.1 (replacement) -> 64.6 (online, thr 0) -> 65.0 (thr 0.5) LaSOT AUC.
distractor_representation: Explicit: every candidate above 0.05 gets a persistent object id and is tracked across frames (separate 'tracks' inside the search window); distractors are also implicit negatives in the DiMP filter via hard-negative updates.
refusal_evidence_horizon: Accumulation over frames: identity continuity across consecutive frames plus a history-max score for switching; refusal (none) itself is decided per frame from the current best score (< 0.25) once the target id is lost.
loss_on_applied_decision: Partly: the loss is on the candidate assignment matrix (association), which is an intermediate step; the applied target selection rule (history-max, thresholds) is hand-designed and not trained; final box and presence are not in the loss.
association_entry_point: Not applicable in the original (single-object). For our use: centre correction of the track prediction before matching (state update input) with refusal = no correction; could alternatively enter the matching cost as a candidate-consistency term.
no_fly_control_equivalent: Same candidate-association pipeline on R1 eye-input features (grey hexals), and a geometry+score-only variant (no appearance); external guard without any association: Kalman gating of the corrected centre, maximum shift relative to box size, and an IoU/cost check that rejects corrections that make the previously matched detection unmatchable. MASA appearance embedding of detections is a second no-fly alternative for 'keep the same object'.
hard_subset_evaluation: No separate hard subset like DiDi; LaSOTExtSub (unseen classes) and attribute subsets (e.g., background clutter, full occlusion, out-of-view) on LaSOT; selection by dataset attribute labels, not by distractor similarity.
temporal_information_availability: Uses only current and previous frames (causal, online); association runs between frame t-1 and t, history kept as id-level max scores and memory. Answer available with zero added latency (18.3 FPS on RTX 2080Ti, 29.6 FPS fast variant). No future-frame selection, so its benefit corresponds to a correction our tracker could apply immediately.
depth_level: Full analysis (code, ablations, all fields) as set in the item.
